ng.headline: Naira holds at N1,364.83 official as parallel rate steadies at N1,405
ng.body: The naira was broadly stable against the dollar on 14 August in both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market and the parallel market. The official NFEM rate stood at N1,364.83 per dollar while the parallel market traded near N1,405 in Lagos and other major cities, leaving a spread of about N40.
ng.why: The gap between official and street rates is what importers and anyone receiving remittances actually pay.

ng.headline: Nigeria's external reserves reach 17-year high of $52.19bn, up 28.4%
ng.body: External reserves rose to $52.19 billion as of 12 August, a 17-year high, according to Central Bank figures. That is 28.39% above the $40.65 billion held in the same period of 2025.
ng.why: Deeper reserves give the central bank more room to defend the naira and clear foreign exchange backlogs.

ng.headline: Naira rises after CBN lifts FX and securities limits on discount window
ng.body: The naira strengthened after the Central Bank of Nigeria removed foreign exchange and securities restrictions on its discount window, BusinessDay reported. Analysts said near-term performance would turn on foreign exchange inflows, crude earnings, diaspora remittances and central bank liquidity management.
ng.why: Easier access to the discount window affects bank liquidity and, through it, lending rates.

ke.headline: Shilling steady at 129.15/35 to the dollar as demand weakens
ke.body: Commercial banks quoted the shilling at 129.15/35 to the dollar, with traders expecting little change in coming sessions. Demand for dollars has weakened, and inflows from investors buying Kenyan government bonds have supported the currency.
ke.why: A stable shilling holds import and fuel costs steady for households and businesses.

ke.headline: Kenya's economy grew 5.3% in the first quarter of 2026
ke.body: The economy expanded 5.3% in the first quarter of 2026, supported by stronger performance in manufacturing, construction, tourism and other service sectors.
ke.why: Growth at this pace underpins tax revenue and the pace of formal hiring.

ke.headline: Forex reserves climb to $15.4bn, strengthening the shilling
ke.body: Kenya's foreign exchange reserves rose to $15.4 billion, with the Central Bank of Kenya pointing to reserve accumulation as a driver behind the shilling's recent gains against the dollar, The Kenya Times reported.
ke.why: Reserve cover determines how long the central bank can smooth the exchange rate if inflows stall.

ke.headline: Treasury forecasts 5.1% growth in 2027 but warns on fuel and the shilling
ke.body: The National Treasury projects economic growth of 5.1% in 2027, while flagging fuel prices and pressure on the shilling as risks to that outlook, Kenyans.co.ke reported.
ke.why: Treasury forecasts set the revenue assumptions behind the next budget and any new borrowing.

eg.headline: Egypt inflation quickens to 14.9% in July, first rise since March
eg.body: Urban consumer prices rose 14.9% year on year in July, up from 14.3% in June, Bloomberg reported. It was the first acceleration since March, breaking an easing trend that had held through much of the ongoing regional conflict.
eg.why: Faster inflation erodes wages and pushes back the point at which borrowing costs start to fall.

eg.headline: Central bank holds overnight deposit rate at 19% for a second meeting
eg.body: The Monetary Policy Committee kept key rates unchanged at its third meeting of the year, a second consecutive hold. The overnight deposit rate stayed at 19% and the overnight lending rate at 20%, with the main operation and discount rates at 19.5%.
eg.why: Rates at these levels keep credit expensive for businesses and mortgage borrowers.

eg.headline: CBE expects inflation to accelerate through the third quarter before easing
eg.body: The Central Bank of Egypt expects annual headline inflation to accelerate through the third quarter of 2026 before declining gradually toward its target. It attributed the path to unfavourable base effects, supply-side pressure from regional conflict, exchange-rate movements and fiscal adjustment.
eg.why: The central bank's own forecast signals how long households should expect price pressure to last.

eg.headline: Egypt growth outlook cut to 5% as inflation delays rate cuts
eg.body: BMI lowered its Egypt growth forecast to 5%, citing persistent inflation that is postponing interest rate cuts, Arab News reported.
eg.why: A slower growth path with rates held high narrows room for job creation.
